newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Paris stocks slip on EU uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Paris stocks slip on EU uncertainty.

text.p: Paris stocks fell from an early trading peak in morning dealings on Monday amid nerves about the Amsterdam EU summit, while other European bourses were mixed, with London shedding nearly one percent.
In currency markets, the dollar slipped slightly against the mark on profit-taking.

Recent dollar gains have been prompted by traders betting that rosier prospects for launching a single European currency would result in a soft euro, making "safe haven" currencies like the dollar an attractive investment.

Much of the day's attention was focused on the volatile Paris bourse. The blue-chip CAC-40 index initially shot up by 0.5 percent to an intra-day high of 2,825.18 points on a wave of optimism about a favourable result from the Amsterdam summit, starting on Monday.

But the mood changed in late morning and stocks went into reverse, barely staying in the plus column by lunch, as investors decided to sit on their hands ahead of declarations expected later from the European leaders.
Brokers said the Paris bourse, hit badly by the Socialists' election win earlier this month, could again react sharply to disappointing news after its strong recent advance.

French investors pushed into the background their hopes for a job-creating pact to come out of Amsterdam and failed to take much comfort from a record-breaking run on Wall Street last week, analysts said.

European leaders were expected to try to accommodate France's Socialist-led government with a form of words stressing the importance of creating work under European economic and monetary union (EMU) without making the kind of changes to a stability pact on fiscal discipline that would upset Germany.

London made the weakest showing. An impressive stock market debut for insurer Norwich Union and the rally in New York failed to outweigh nerves ahead of the new British government's first budget and the EU summit.
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares, which set three closing records last week, fell 43.4 to 4,739.7 points.
Last week's bullish mood was dented by talk that dividend tax benefits might be axed in the budget on July 2 in a move that would target the corporate sector rather than cooling consumer spending
"It's certainly not as joyous a scene as last Friday," said Ian Williams, equities strategist at Panmure Gordon. "It has pulled the rug from under the market's feet.
"It will put a lid on things until we hear what (Chancellor Gordon) Brown intends to do."
Traders said uncertainty ahead of the budget was likely to cause volatility in the short term. Concern over the European Union summit was also dampening sentiment, they said.
One bright spot in the market was Norwich Union's market debut. Shares in the former mutually-owned insurance group opened at 356p, compared with a public offer price of 290p.
In Frankfurt, stocks made healthy gains, lifted by a near one percent jump on Wall Street on Friday and the firmer tone of the dollar, seen as helping the German exporting sector.
The DAX-30 index put on over 0.5 percent in early trade to 3,770.90 points at one point but volume was weak.

"Basically there isn't a whole lot around to talk about this morning. We're higher on the back of Wall Street and we could reach 3,800 points during bourse trade. Turnover is very thin," a Frankfurt broker said.
In currencies, the dollar slipped against the yen, as worries over U.S.-Japan trade frictions refused to go away, but held last week's gains on the mark, although profit-taking made inroads.

The dollar was around 1.7327 marks, still nearly two pfennigs above the levels seen for much of last week, but slipped to 114.06 yen, more than half a yen below the range in late European trading on Friday.
Though accord on the stability pact, which aims to enforce budgetary rigour after EMU begins, is now largely priced in, analysts said a deal should support the dollar.

It was likely to fuel fears that the mark would be swallowed up into a weak single currency. France last week sparked fears of EMU delay -- and a flight into marks -- when it asked for more time to study the pact
"All eyes are on Amsterdam -- that's going to overshadow any data from the U.S. for the next couple of days," said Elizabeth Cheale, trader at Dresdner Bank in London.
The dollar was not expected to make much headway against the yen as last week's worries lingered about U.S.-Japanese trade friction ahead of a Group of Seven (G7) summit in Denver on June 20-22.

The market fears that the trade imbalance could prompt a clash between the U.S. and Japan, although an international monetary source helped calm those concerns by saying G7 leaders might not single out Japan's surplus for attention.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7327 marks and 114.06 yen, compared with 1.7373 and 114.73 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 43.0 points at 4,740.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 1.01 at 2809.53.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 20.67 at 3,765.11.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.95 an ounce, compared with Friday's close of $341.55. Silver was down two cents at $4.71.
